title: Investigating sources of inaccuracy in wearable optical heart rate sensors
authors: Bent B, Goldstein BA, Kibbe WA, Dunn JP
population: Consumer- and research-grade wearables tested across skin tones and activity types (sample size not in the abstract)
findings: The authors saw no statistically significant difference in HR accuracy across skin tones.
They did see significant differences between devices and between activity types; absolute error during activity was on average 30% higher than during rest.
Wearables were all reasonably accurate at rest and at prolonged elevated heart rate, but differed in responding to changes in activity.
limitations: Abstract gives no sample size, device list or error in bpm; mostly laboratory conditions; the result on skin tone was contested in published Matters Arising (Colvonen 2021; reply Bent 2021) whose content was not read.
implications: Supports modelling wrist-HR quality per device and per activity change rather than per skin tone, consistent with the inconclusive systematic review (Koerber).
HR during changing intensity (intervals, hills) deserves lower confidence than steady running.
